transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-04-23 11:00 PDT | Duration: ~42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Sofia Ramos (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (OrbitalAI ML Eng), Ethan Cole (OrbitalAI Product), Danielle Wu (OrbitalAI Infra), Joel Park (CTO - joined late)
---
Summary: quick weekly POC sync focused on economics (tokens/sec/$), caching wins, and batching tradeoffs. SE shared interim benchmark numbers; customer asked about tail latency and security implications for Dedicated. Action items captured at end.
Topics: cost per token math, observed tokens/sec with/without prefix KV caching, batching sweet spot, quantization impact on latency, pilot scope for procurement decision.
Artifacts referenced: cost-model-v2.xlsx (https://redwood.example/cost-model-v2.xlsx), perf-profiles/kv-cache-results.csv (shared by Marcus), demo-recording-link (placeholder)
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (AE): okay hi everyone thanks for joining, this is the weekly pilot check-in for OrbitalAI. quick run through agenda: econ review, perf numbers, open asks. Marcus will start with the bench highlights.
[00:18] Marcus (SE): thanks sofia. I ran the microbench yesterday on the hosted instance using the customer model snapshot v2. We measured raw gen throughput at about 1,800 tokens/sec on a single A100-like instance with default 16-bit float. With prefix caching enabled we saw an effective tokens/sec to the app of roughly 3,200 — so about +78% improvement on throughput for our sample workload.
[00:40] Priya (Customer): sorry can you repeat the 3,200 number? is that tokens per second or requests?
[00:45] Marcus: tokens per second. that's after we allowed prefix reuse and a small KV hit rate of ~42%. the caveat: the sample has a lot of repeated system prompts so your hit rate might be higher when you annotate prefixes.
[01:02] Ethan: what's the cost delta look like in dollars? like tokens per dollar?
[01:06] Marcus: right — we computed tokens/sec/$ using the hosted rate assumptions in the cost sheet. baseline (no caching, batch=1) is about 25k tokens per dollar; with caching and batch=8 that moves to roughly 44k tokens per dollar. again these are illustrative — depends on seq lengths.
[01:30] Danielle: when you say batch=8 what's the p50 latency? tail latency?
[01:35] Marcus: good question. batch=8 gives p50 ~95ms per request, p95 ~320ms. batch=32 pushes p50 down slightly to ~70ms for aggregated token throughput but p95 rises to ~560ms in our runs — so tail suffers. for customer-facing interactive flows we recommend batch=8 as a tradeoff.
[02:05] Priya: that aligns with our SLA — anything over 400ms p95 will feel sluggish to users.
[02:10] Sofia: quick note on dedicated vs hosted: dedicated lowers per-token unit cost in sustained traffic patterns because of reserved capacity pricing, but you lose some flexibility. we put a delta table in the cost-model sheet.
[02:25] Joel (CTO, joined): hi all, sorry I'm late — heard we got big caching wins, what's needed from infra?
[02:33] Marcus: hey joel — main ask: if you run the pilot in your VPC/private deployment please ensure the inference nodes can access the prefix cache store with low latency (we recommend colocated NVMe or a low-latency redis cluster). otherwise KV cache hit latency kills the benefit.
[02:50] Danielle: we can stand up a redis cluster in the same AZ, we just need to confirm EBS optimization for the instances if we do private.
[02:58] Marcus: perfect. also note our KV cache prototype is tolerant of transient misses, and there's a graceful fallback to model-only path. we saw about 12% extra compute overhead for cache coordination at high concurrency.
[03:18] Ethan: can you explain the tokens/sec/$ calc end-to-end? i've got a hard time mapping it to customer pricing.
[03:25] Marcus: sure — it's basically throughput (tokens/sec) times service uptime seconds per dollar. more concretely: tokens/sec * 3600 * 24 * 30 gives tokens/hour-day-month scaled; divide by monthly spend on the instance to get tokens per dollar. in the sheet we normalize to a 1-month sustained run.
[03:50] Priya: and do you account for cache storage costs?
[03:53] Marcus: yes included as a small monthly cost in the delta. for our numbers the cache storage added about 4% to infra cost but reduced compute by ~30% net, so overall net savings ~25% in cost/month for this workload.
[04:12] Sofia: wanted to highlight quantization: Marcus ran int8 and 4-bit quant tests. 4-bit (q4) gave a ~1.6x improvement in tokens/sec but with a perceptible quality drop on long-context generation; int8 was milder, ~1.2x with no measurable quality regression on the eval set.
[04:36] Priya: we care about hallucination rate on our product; can we get evals on the 5k prompt set?
[04:41] Marcus: yes that's why we asked for the 5k sample. once we run the q configs we'll produce automated eval metrics (perplexity, ROUGE-ish proxies, hallucination markers) and share.
[04:55] Ethan: any concerns with quantization + KV cache interaction?
[04:59] Marcus: minor — quantization affects inference kernel performance; cache keys are model-version + prefix hash so behaviour is orthogonal, but performance knobs differ per quant profile. we'll include kernel selection notes in the perf report.
[05:15] Priya: can you show the raw numbers you referenced earlier? the 25k -> 44k tokens/$
[05:19] Marcus: yes open cost-model-v2.xlsx, sheet 'summary'. baseline host (batch1, no cache, fp16) = 25k tokens/$; host with cache & batch8 = 44k; dedicated reserved with cache = ~62k tokens/$ at 70% utilization.
[05:39] Sophie? (transcript glitch — speaker mislabelled): uh that dedicated number assumes year commitment right?
[05:44] Sofia: yes that's with a 12-month reserved commitment and the reserved discount. there's also a blended contract if you want burst capacity on hosted for peak times.
[05:55] Danielle: procurement will want the SKU/instance types and exact numbers for cost modeling.
[05:58] Sofia: we'll send SKU list and the assumptions as a single table.
[06:02] Ethan: about batching — we're worried about variable prompt lengths. how aggressive do you recommend?
[06:06] Marcus: for heavy variance we recommend adaptive batching: set a max batch window of ~20ms and max batch size 8. that keeps latency mostly bounded while still collecting coalesced work. in our internal runs adaptive batching picked up ~1.4x throughput on average with <10% added p95.
[06:27] Priya: is there support for prefix annotation in the SDK or do we need to rewrite prompts?
[06:32] Marcus: SDK supports prefix hints; we'll send sample code. you can also do server-side hinting if you can't change client requests.
[06:40] Priya: great. also, one of our concerns is rate limiting and throttles from multi-tenant hosted env. any fallback strategy?
[06:47] Sofia: yes we propose a policy: primary route to hosted model, fallback to a smaller quantized variant or dedicated pool depending on SLA. Redwood console supports automated route policy.
[06:58] Ethan: curious — how do you measure real user cost? tokens don't capture downstream post-processing and embeddings calls.
[07:05] Marcus: agreed. the cost-model includes a line for post-processing CPU and an embedding uplifts line. for your flows embeddings are a small fraction (avg 8% of total).
[07:20] Priya: can we get an example of the billing breakdown per feature?
[07:23] Sofia: yes we'll slice the cost model by route: gen, embeddings, rerank. we'll also show token vs embedding split.
[07:30] Marcus: quick note on the KV hit rate sensitivity: we ran a sweep from 10% to 70% hit rates. the net compute reduction scales roughly linearly; above ~50% hits you get diminishing returns as retrieval overhead increases. so the sweet spot is often 30-50% for many apps.
[07:55] Priya: what about data residency / retention — storing prefixes, any compliance issue?
[08:00] Sofia: good point. Redwood can configure cache TTLs and encryption-at-rest. for regulated data you can disable persistent caching, or use short TTLs and audit logs. the private deployment supports customer-managed KMS.
[08:13] Danielle: we'll want SOC2 artifact and configuration checklist for private.
[08:17] Sofia: will attach security docs in the follow-up email.
[08:20] Ethan: also can you remind us what the procurement milestones look like to move to Dedicated?
[08:24] Sofia: generally a pilot -> dedicated proof point requiring 30-60 day commitment thresholds, procurement paperwork, and a technical cutover plan. we'll provide a procurement checklist.
[08:33] Marcus: returning to perf, one oddity: we saw an outlier p99 spike when cache eviction occurred under high churn; investigating LRU tuning reduced that spike by ~40%. we'll include eviction config recommendations.
[08:50] Priya: thanks — eviction behavior is a key operational concern for us.
[08:54] Marcus: also ran a cost-sensitivity for quantization: q4 improved tokens/$ by 60% but reduced eval-quality score by ~4 points on your hallucination metric. int8 had a 22% tokens/$ improvement with <1% quality delta.
[09:18] Ethan: so intuitively we should pilot int8 first on less-critical routes, and q4 for background batch jobs?
[09:23] Marcus: exactly. that's what we recommend.
[09:27] Joel: quick infra note — if we go private we need to ensure GPU drivers and kernel modules match the redwood runtime; what's the upgrade cadence?
[09:35] Marcus: we publish compatibility matrix in the distro; minor patches monthly, major runtime updates quarterly with backward-compatible model variants.
[09:46] Priya: any blockers from your side to run the 10k benchmark?
[09:49] Marcus: need the annotated prompts and an allowlist for test endpoints; Sofia will send an access token.
[09:56] Sofia: i'll issue short-lived pilot token and add Marcus to the OrbitalAI test workspace.
[10:00] Ethan: timeline — when do you think we'll have full bench results and a cost recommendation?
[10:04] Marcus: bench by 2025-04-29, report by 2025-04-30. procurement-ready pricing table by 2025-05-02.
[10:12] Priya: sounds good. 
[10:15] Sofia: any final q's?
[10:18] Priya: none from me. thanks all.
[10:21] Ethan: thanks.
[10:22] Danielle: thanks.
[10:23] Joel: thanks, talk soon.
---
Recap (readout):
- Benchmarks show caching and batching drive most of the initial unit-economics improvement; expected tokens/$: baseline 25k -> cached/batch8 44k -> dedicated 62k at 70% util.
- Latency tradeoffs: batch size ~8 recommended for interactive flows; adaptive batching recommended for variable prompt sizes.
- Quantization: int8 recommended for initial rollout; q4 for background/batch jobs after eval.
- Security/compliance: private deployment supports KMS and cache TTL controls; Redwood to share SOC2 docs.
Action items: see action_items above.
End of transcript.
